title: Method Teardown
description: Pass-2 method teardown of ONE read paper. The structured breakdown of how the paper's method actually works: the problem it defines, the assumptions that must hold, the representation/search-space/objective it changes, the per-term loss with 'what deleting it does', the train/infer flow, the data, the cost, and the single mechanism that differs from the baseline. source_ref-anchored; rendered into the DB paper page. A reading aid — never a governed gate.

source_ref.description: the paper this teardown reads (matches the paper_note / DB page source_ref)

problem_definition.description: the input/output/target and task boundary — what the method takes in, what it produces, what it is and is not solving

core_assumptions.description: what must hold for the method to work (data, modeling, or deployment assumptions)

representation.description: what structure, search-space, or objective the method changes relative to the prior art

loss_terms.description: per-term loss decomposition; ablate_effect records 'what deleting this term does'

term.description: name of the loss term, e.g. 'Dice', 'boundary', 'L_consistency'

role.description: what this term is meant to enforce

ablate_effect.description: the observed (or stated) effect of removing this term

training_flow.description: how the method is trained: stages, inputs, supervision, optimization

inference_flow.description: how the method runs at inference: inputs, passes, post-processing

train_infer_consistency.description: whether train-time and inference-time conditions match, and any train/infer gap that could distort results

data.description: source/scale/splits and the leakage risk of the data used

baseline_difference.description: the one mechanism that changed versus the baseline — the single causal delta that the paper claims drives the improvement
